steps.title: Before any run: build, freeze, audit
steps.plain: The data layers are built once (public ids, the hub-to-facility map, the disruption bindings, the concept map). Then every file an agent will ever see is hashed into a frozen manifest, and an audit checks that the four topologies get a fair, identical treatment surface.

steps.title: 1 · The harness opens the run
steps.plain: A run folder is created, the task specification is delivered word for word, and layer L1 (the network) is granted. From now on every tool call is logged with a receipt id.

steps.title: 2 · Plan checkpoint
steps.plain: The team queries the network, routes month by month, and assembles its report with the report tools. finalize_report submits it; the save gate rejects any report with invented ids or citations the run never received.

steps.title: 3 · The disruption arrives (L2)
steps.plain: The harness delivers the operator notice for D2 and grants layer L2. Two new tools appear: one re-serves the notice, the other says which of the team's own ids the disruption affects.

steps.title: 4 · Revision checkpoint
steps.plain: The team carries its plan forward and changes only what the notice changes: reroute with perturb, move facilities an affected hub served to another route or to unserved, log every claim whose status changed.

steps.title: 5 · Context documents are released (L3)
steps.plain: Socio-economic documents are unlocked, as context tends to arrive late in real planning. The harness also pushes a few passages found along the saved routes, each with a receipt to cite.

steps.title: 6 · Reassessment checkpoint
steps.plain: The team confirms, changes or defers each decision in the light of the documents. Leaving the plan unchanged is a valid outcome; an empty revision log records that choice.

steps.title: 7 · The run is sealed
steps.plain: The runner hashes the reports into the run summary manifest, classifies any failure, and renders a PDF with maps so a person can read the run by eye.

steps.title: 8 · Scoring and the blind judge
steps.plain: Deterministic scorers check completion, grounding (every citation against the tool log), the revision against the disruption's hidden answer key, continuity and seasonal validity. A separate model judges each report blind, without knowing the topology.

steps.title: 9 · Archive
steps.plain: Each arm is archived with a README, a card per run, the reports, the scores and the read-out, so the study can be re-read later.
